sec: Thyrotoxicosis vs Euthyroid Hyperthyroxinemia & Iodine Effects

items.q: How does page 910 distinguish thyrotoxicosis from euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia in patients with elevated T3 and T4 levels?
opts: Thyrotoxicosis has elevated free T3 and free T4, whereas euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia has elevated total T3 and total T4
Thyrotoxicosis has suppressed total hormones, whereas euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia has elevated free hormones
Thyrotoxicosis has normal free hormones, whereas euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia has elevated free T4 only
Thyrotoxicosis always features high TSH, whereas euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia features low TSH
items.exp: Hyperthyroxinemia (↑ T3, ↑ T4) branches into: ↑ free T3, T4 = Thyrotoxicosis; and ↑ total T3, T4 = Euthyroid Hyperthyroxinemia. (Book p910)

items.q: Under thyrotoxicosis, match the functional gland status to its etiologies — 1) Overworking thyroid gland (Hyperthyroidism) 2) Normal working thyroid gland … A) Autoimmune Graves (m/c), Nodular toxic adenoma, Toxic MNG, TSH adenoma, Struma ovarii B) Thyroiditis, Thyrotoxicosis factitia, Amiodarone
items.exp: Overworking gland includes Graves, toxic adenoma, toxic MNG, TSH adenoma, and struma ovarii; normal gland includes thyroiditis, factitia, and amiodarone. (Book p910)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed under euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia (↑ total T3, T4) on page 910?
opts: Deiodinase deficiency and Sick Euthyroid syndrome
items.exp: Struma ovarii is a cause of thyrotoxicosis from an overworking gland; euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia includes TBG excess, RTH, deiodinase deficiency, and sick euthyroid syndrome. (Book p910)

items.q: What percentage of all thyrotoxicosis cases are caused by Graves' disease on page 910?
items.exp: Under Graves disease Features: '75% Thyrotoxicosis cases -> Graves disease'. (Book p910)

items.q: What is the peak population age and gender predilection for Graves' disease?
items.exp: Under Graves disease: 'Population at risk : 20-50 years (F > m)'. (Book p910)

items.q: Match the clinical risk associations of Graves' disease — 1) Lifestyle factor 2) Reproductive period 3) Antiviral therapy … A) Smoking B) Post partum C) HAART (Highly active antiretroviral therapy)
items.exp: Associations listed on page 910 for Graves' disease include: Smoking, Post partum, HAART, and HLA: DR-2, CTLA-4, PTPN-22. (Book p910)

items.q: Regarding immunogenetic associations of Graves' disease on page 910: I HLA association is HLA-DR2. II Non-HLA gene associations include CTLA-4 and PTPN-22.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Under Graves disease: 'HLA : DR-2, CTLA-4, PTPN-22'. (Book p910)

items.q: The Wolff-Chaikoff effect occurs when excess iodide transiently inhibits thyroid synthesis for ___ days, followed by ___.
items.exp: Wolff Chaikoff effect: 'Excess iodide -> Inhibits Transiently Thyroid synthesis (5-7 days) -> Followed by Escape'. (Book p910)

items.q: Which medication is specifically noted on page 910 as precipitating the Wolff-Chaikoff effect?
items.exp: Under Wolff Chaikoff effect: 'Seen with Amiodarone'. (Book p910)

items.q: A patient with nodular thyroid disease residing in an iodine-deficient area receives an iodine-containing radiographic contrast agent and promptly develops thyrotoxicosis. What iodine-induced disorder explains this?
items.exp: Jod Basedow phenomenon: 'Patient with Nodular or TSH-R Antibody in iodine deficient area -> Iodine Supply (+) -> Thyrotoxicosis'. (Book p910)

items.q: Assess these two iodine-related effects: I Wolff-Chaikoff effect is transient synthesis inhibition by excess iodide (seen with amiodarone). II Jod-Basedow phenomenon is thyrotoxicosis induced by iodine supply in patients with nodular disease or TSH-R antibodies in iodine-deficient areas.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Both statements represent the exact definitions of the Wolff-Chaikoff effect and Jod-Basedow phenomenon on page 910. (Book p910)

items.q: Which of the following causes of thyrotoxicosis represents ectopic thyroid tissue outside the neck?
items.exp: Struma ovarii is an ovarian teratoma containing functioning thyroid tissue that causes hyperthyroidism. (Book p910)
